answer.label: Written in
answer.sourceLine: This is a genuine verse: Proverbs 17:17 in the King James Version (1611), confirmed word-for-word against multiple KJV texts. The English wording is the King James translators’ rendering of the Hebrew of Proverbs; modern translations reword the same verse (e.g. “A friend loves at all times”).

source.excerpt: A friend loveth at all times, and a brother is born for adversity.
trail: The exact KJV wording is confirmed at Bible Hub’s KJV text ↗: “A friend loveth at all times, and a brother is born for adversity.”
King James Bible Online ↗ prints the identical verse for Proverbs 17:17.

Modern translations render the same Hebrew verse differently — e.g. the NLT’s “A friend is always loyal, and a brother is born to help in time of need” (Bible.com ↗) — so the archaic “loveth…born for adversity” phrasing is specifically the King James wording.
source.excerptNote: The verse as printed in the King James Version of Proverbs 17:17.
source.rightsNote: The King James Version was first published in 1611 (the standard modern text is the 1769 Blayney revision), far earlier than 1931, so the English wording is public domain in the United States. (In the United Kingdom the KJV is under perpetual Crown copyright, but that does not affect US public-domain status.)

author.name: King James Bible (Book of Proverbs)
author.heading: About the source
author.metaLine: Proverbs 17:17 · King James Version, first published 1611
author.bio: The Book of Proverbs is a collection of Hebrew wisdom sayings in the Old Testament, traditionally associated with King Solomon. The King James Version (Authorized Version) was produced by a body of English scholars and first published in 1611; its stately English gave this verse the enduring form “A friend loveth at all times, and a brother is born for adversity.”

misattribution.heading: Often misattributed
misattribution.intro: The credit here is essentially correct — this is a real Bible verse. The main thing worth flagging is wording, not authorship.

items.why: The archaic phrasing “loveth at all times…born for adversity” belongs specifically to the King James Version. Modern versions reword the same verse — the NLT reads “A friend is always loyal, and a brother is born to help in time of need” (Bible.com ↗). Quoting the KJV form is genuine; attributing that exact phrasing to a modern translation would be inaccurate.

misattribution.truthLine: Genuine and correctly credited: it is Proverbs 17:17 in the King James Version ↗, confirmed verbatim.

context.heading: Why it endures
lead: Proverbs 17:17 is one of the Bible’s most-quoted lines on friendship and loyalty. The two clauses work as a Hebrew parallelism: a true friend loves consistently — “at all times” — and a brother (or kinsman) proves himself precisely when trouble comes.

The King James wording, with its “loveth” and “born for adversity,” is the form that circulates on cards, sermons and memorials, which is why it is worth pinning to the specific 1611 translation rather than a later paraphrase.
